+# Navigation visual references (#751)
+
+These eight initial images are **candidates pending explicit human approval**.
+Pixel equality is separate from accepting a reference as correct. The CI approval
+gate must pass before QA acceptance. No implementation agent may post approval.
+
+| Original | Observable case |
+| --- | --- |
+| [Empty scanner](empty-scanner.png) | Seeded universe before the first scan, no catalog leak |
+| [Visible contacts](visible-contacts.png) | Four distinct faceted bodies, fixed front camera |
+| [Panning](panned-contacts.png) | Real D-key camera movement, bodies retained |
+| [Selected body](selected-body.png) | Moon picker selection and selection geometry |
+| [Zoom out](zoom-out.png) | Fixed zoom 0.1, linear world projection |
+| [Zoom in](zoom-in.png) | Fixed zoom 1, readable proxies |
+| [Heading/velocity](heading-velocity.png) | Yellow heading right, green dashed velocity up |
+| [Opposite vectors](opposite-vectors.png) | Heading and velocity reach opposite edges |
+
+Full 1280×800 viewport images include the actual WebGL canvas, DOM vector overlay
+and sidebar layout. No masks, cropping, dynamic substitutions or CSS geometry
+changes are applied. Vendored, licensed DejaVu fonts supply the fixture's `Inter`
+family to avoid host fallback changes. Ordinary production and browser tests still
+exercise system fonts; this fixture CSS does not ship in the production entry.
+
+## Compare and retain evidence
+
+```sh
+npm ci
+npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
+npm run build
+npm run test:visual
+SALIMON_EVIDENCE_DIR=test-results/visual-repeat npm run test:visual
+npm run test:visual:negative
+```
+
+Use the lockfile Chromium on Linux x64; do not set `CHROMIUM_PATH` for reference
+qualification. Environment drift (browser/Playwright/platform/architecture/font
+hashes/renderer) fails explicitly. Chromium explicitly disables LCD text
+(`--disable-lcd-text`) so opaque sidebar glyphs use the same grayscale
+rasterization on Debian and Ubuntu. Actual launch flags are recorded per capture. Host distro/version is recorded in the issue
+report/CI runner rather than asserting Debian and Ubuntu are the same OS.
+Seed 750, fixture front camera, fixed zooms, DPR 1, en-US/UTC, dark scheme and
+paused RAF/performance clock are recorded in `manifest.json` and observations.
+The capture waits for fonts and completed production frames. Screenshot capture
+never fast-forwards animations. Traces are retained even on success.
+
+`comparisons/` under each test output contains actual, expected, diff and original
+state/metadata JSON for every case. The summary records changed and raw changed
+pixels and both hashes. Pixelmatch uses color threshold 0.1, includes antialiasing,
+and permits **zero** pixels over threshold. No mask is justified by these frozen
+scenes. CI uploads SHA-named originals/diffs/metadata/traces for 14 days; essential
+issue evidence is retained beside the delivery report. A page error, environment
+change, absent contacts, wrong selection or corrupted/missing reference fails.
+
+The negative driver changes the actual velocity CSS to red in a disposable copy.
+Only the two velocity-visible frames must fail, with >100 changed pixels each;
+the other six must pass. Timeout, startup error or unrelated visual failures do
+not count as detecting the defect. It never edits checkout references.
+
+## Propose and independently approve a baseline
+
+1. First investigate the unexpected difference. Never update references merely
+   because a check fails. Browser/OS upgrades are separate deliberate changes;
+   retain old and new originals, environment versions, metrics and upgrade reason.
+2. Generate *candidates* outside the tracked reference directory:
+   `SALIMON_CAPTURE_CANDIDATES=/tmp/navigation-candidates npm run test:visual`.
+   Candidate generation is forbidden in CI. `--update-snapshots` has no effect on
+   this custom comparator and cannot update these files.
+3. Copy reviewed candidates and their complete `manifest.json` into this directory
+   in a dedicated reviewable change. Run normal comparisons twice and the negative
+   driver; preserve the previous originals in git and expected/diff artifacts.
+4. A human repository OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR independently reviews every image,
+   environment/threshold change, functional tests and diff. Post exactly this on
+   the delivering PR, substituting the SHA-256 of the **manifest bytes**:
+   `Approve navigation baselines: <sha256>`.
+   Agents must never write this comment, impersonate the reviewer or count their
+   own image judgment as approval. The human can use the same GitHub account that
+   hosts an agent-authored PR; independence is from the implementing agent.
+5. Rerun the failed `baseline-approval` job (the successful browser/build job does
+   not need to run again). It validates image hashes and accepts only
+   that exact digest from a human collaborator (Bot/unaffiliated accounts fail).
+   Any changed manifest invalidates the approval. A byte-identical manifest
+   inherited from the PR base needs no repeat approval. Baseline approval does
+   not replace independent implementation QA or authorize merging.
+
+GitHub branch protection must require the Navigation client check for enforcement
+at merge; this issue does not change repository administration settings. A repo
+maintainer can always alter workflow policy; ordinary implementation agents cannot
+waive it. Review comments are audit evidence, not a cryptographic proof of who
+operated an account. Required human decisions stay visible as BLOCKED until made.
+
+Software SwiftShader browser coverage does not qualify physical input, discrete
+GPUs, Metal, Windows rendering, native platforms, hardware FPS or subjective art.
+Historical native mesh regression #228 is a distinct renderer/asset contract.

index 0000000..f52f0d1
--- /dev/null
+++ b/client/tests/navigation-captures.spec.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+import {test,expect} from '@playwright/test'
+import {readFile,writeFile,mkdir} from 'node:fs/promises'
+import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process'
+import {join} from 'node:path'
+import {boot,snapshot,json,EPOCH} from './deterministic'
+import {POLICY,sha256,compareImages} from '../scripts/visual-comparison.ts'
+
+const directory='tests/navigation-baselines'
+const candidate=process.env.SALIMON_CAPTURE_CANDIDATES||undefined
+if(candidate&&process.env.CI)throw Error('Candidate generation is forbidden in CI')
+const cases=[
+ {id:'empty-scanner',scenario:'seeded-empty',vector:'zero'},
+ {id:'visible-contacts'},
+ {id:'panned-contacts',pan:true},
+ {id:'selected-body',selected:true},
+ {id:'zoom-out',zoom:.1},
+ {id:'zoom-in',zoom:1},
+ {id:'heading-velocity',vector:'different'},
+ {id:'opposite-vectors',vector:'opposite'}
+] as const
+// One ordered session preserves a single manifest and complete comparison summary.
+test('VIS-1/2 eight navigation screens match reference pixels',async({page,browser},info)=>{
+ const errors:string[]=[];page.on('pageerror',e=>errors.push(e.message))
+ const fonts=await Promise.all(['DejaVuSans.ttf','DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf','fonts.css'].map(async f=>[f,sha256(await readFile(`tests/assets/${f}`))]))
+ const launchArgs=info.project.use.launchOptions?.args??[]
+ expect(launchArgs,'VISUAL_RASTERIZATION_POLICY').toContain('--disable-lcd-text')
+ const source=(await readFile('.revision-for-negative','utf8').catch(()=>null))??execFileSync('git',['rev-parse','HEAD'],{encoding:'utf8'}).trim()
+ const environment={platform:process.platform,arch:process.arch,browser:browser.version(),playwright:JSON.parse(await readFile('node_modules/@playwright/test/package.json','utf8')).version,viewport:{width:1280,height:800},dpr:1,locale:'en-US',timezone:'UTC',colorScheme:'dark',fontHashes:Object.fromEntries(fonts),seed:750,epoch:EPOCH,policy:POLICY}
+ const manifest=candidate?null:JSON.parse(await readFile(`${directory}/manifest.json`,'utf8'))
+ const results:Record<string,unknown>[]=[],images:Record<string,string>={}
+ const output=candidate??info.outputPath('comparisons')
+ await mkdir(output,{recursive:true})
+ // Drift is a failure, never an instruction to regenerate references.
+ if(manifest)expect(environment,'VISUAL_ENVIRONMENT_DRIFT: propose separately reviewed candidates').toEqual(manifest.environment)
+ for(const fixture of cases) {
+  const c:{id:string;scenario?:string;vector?:string;pan?:boolean;selected?:boolean;zoom?:number}=fixture
+  await boot(page,`scenario=${c.scenario??'seeded'}&seed=750&view=front&vector=${c.vector??'zero'}&zoom=${c.zoom??.5}`)
+  await page.evaluate(()=>document.fonts.ready)
+  if(c.selected)await page.getByLabel('Scanned contacts (4)',{exact:true}).selectOption('moon')
+  if(c.pan){await page.keyboard.down('d');await page.clock.runFor(160);await page.keyboard.up('d')}
+  // Deterministic completed RAF; no screenshot animation fast-forward or polling
+  // against mutating frames. Font loading completes before this last frame.
+  await page.clock.runFor(32)
+  await page.mouse.move(1279,799)
+  const state=await snapshot(page)
+  expect(state.scene.renderer,'VISUAL_BACKEND').toContain('SwiftShader')
+  if(manifest)expect(state.scene.renderer,'VISUAL_RENDERER_DRIFT').toBe(manifest.renderer)
+  if(c.scenario==='seeded-empty')expect(state.navigation.pulse).toBe(0)
+  else expect(state.scene.objects.filter(o=>o.name.startsWith('nav-body:')).length,'VISUAL_NONVACUOUS_CONTACTS').toBeGreaterThan(0)
+  if(c.selected)expect(state.navigation.selected).toBe('moon')
+  const actual=await page.screenshot({caret:'hide'})
+  const name=`${c.id}.png`;images[name]=sha256(actual)
+  await writeFile(join(output,name),actual)
+  await writeFile(join(output,`${c.id}.json`),json({source,environment,launchArgs,fixture,state,errors}))
+  await info.attach(name,{body:actual,contentType:'image/png'})
+  if(candidate){results.push({id:c.id,status:'CANDIDATE',sha256:sha256(actual)});continue}
+  const original=await readFile(join(directory,name))
+  expect(sha256(original),'BASELINE_HASH_MISMATCH').toBe(manifest.images[name])
+  const comparison=compareImages(original,actual)
+  await writeFile(join(output,`${c.id}-expected.png`),original)
+  await writeFile(join(output,`${c.id}-diff.png`),comparison.diff)
+  await info.attach(`${c.id}-diff.png`,{body:comparison.diff,contentType:'image/png'})
+  const {diff:_,...measurement}=comparison
+  results.push({id:c.id,...measurement,expected:sha256(original),actual:sha256(actual)})
+ }
+ expect(errors,'VISUAL_PAGE_ERRORS').toEqual([])
+ if(candidate) {
+  const renderer=(await snapshot(page)).scene.renderer
+  await writeFile(join(output,'manifest.json'),json({schema:1,environment,renderer,images})+'\n')
+ }
+ await writeFile(join(output,'summary.json'),json({source,launchArgs,candidate:!!candidate,results})+'\n')
+ await info.attach('comparison-summary.json',{body:json({source,launchArgs,candidate:!!candidate,results}),contentType:'application/json'})
+ // Soft per-frame failures let QA inspect every unexpected screen in one run.
+ for(const r of results)if(!candidate)expect.soft(r.pass,`VISUAL_PIXEL_MISMATCH ${r.id}: ${r.changedPixels} changed pixels`).toBe(true)
+})

+# Cockpit navigation, multiplayer presence and reconnect
+
+**Status:** Approved future gameplay design, 2026-11-04. This document is authoritative for the **strict top-down 2D** player-world / **3D holographic navigation** transition and the disconnect/reconnect behavior discussed here. **Not implemented** in the current navigation-only React client; no multiplayer backend, 2D interior, shared player persistence or ship-interaction runtime is claimed.
+
+Companion contracts: [2D art direction](top-down-art-direction.md), [navigation-only radar prototype](radar-navigation-prototype.md), [multiplayer](multiplayer-and-npc-interaction.md), [spaceship and survival](spaceship-building-and-survival.md), and [legacy save contract](save-contract.md).
+
+## Player view, chair and navigation authority
+
+- The **default actual-world view is strict overhead illustrated 2D**. This includes walking inside the Scout, planetary traversal, mining, storage and module interactions.
+- The **3D navigation radar is an in-world cockpit interface**, not the world representation or an always-available global menu. A player must approach and interact with the cockpit desk to enter it.
+- When an authorized player activates a **powered, unoccupied** cockpit, the player occupies the pilot chair in the 2D world and switches **locally** to the 3D navigation view. Other connected players aboard see that player **seated at the cockpit**, not a vanished character or an avatar inside the radar.
+- Preserve existing **owner-only ship-navigation control** and **one occupant per pilot chair**. Other players may enter the cockpit area and operate other allowed ship systems; observing an occupied chair never grants navigation authority. Multiplayer authority must confirm chair/control acquisition atomically before allowing control.
+- Player world position, cockpit occupancy, local view mode and ship navigation/control ownership are distinct pieces of state. The pilot's radar camera is local presentation; the world communicates seating and ship-control status rather than streaming the pilot's 3D interface to spectators.
+- Entering/leaving the view does **not** reset ship orientation, velocity, throttle or ship time. Ship physics and automatic modules evolve independently of whether the pilot is looking at 3D, walking in 2D, or disconnected, subject to the existing power and offline-flight rules.
+
+## Transition state table
+
+| Event | Local view after transition | Physical character in 2D world | Pilot chair/control |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Normal play / walking | 2D | Standing/moving | No cockpit occupancy |
+| Owner interacts with powered available cockpit desk | 3D navigation | Seated in cockpit chair | Occupied; authorized controls |
+| Pilot exits navigation voluntarily | 2D | **Automatically stands** beside chair | Occupancy and active controls released |
+| Cockpit power fails during navigation | **Automatically 2D** | **Remains seated** | Chair stays occupied; powered controls unavailable |
+| Player stands up from unpowered chair | 2D | Stands (or follows independently approved zero-G movement rules) | Chair released |
+| Power returns while player remains seated | 2D | Remains seated | Navigation **does not reopen automatically** |
+| Seated authorized player explicitly interacts with powered desk again | 3D | Remains seated | Active navigation resumes |
+| Active pilot disconnects | No local view; character removed from shared world | No avatar remains | Interaction aborted; occupancy/control released |
+| Pilot reconnects following an interrupted cockpit interaction | 2D | **Standing next to cockpit** | No active navigation / chair occupancy |
+
+Voluntary exit is **one action** that returns to ordinary movement; it should not require a separate stand-up command. After a forced power-failure return, the player may remain seated or stand, including without powered instruments. Seating visuals/animation should suit the strict top-down art direction, but timing and input bindings are deferred.
+
+If power recovers after blackout, the user **chooses** when to open navigation again. Existing saved ship throttle/propulsion rules remain separate from cockpit screen presentation.
+
+## Multiplayer synchronization and disconnect
+
+- A disconnected player is **removed from the world**: no visible avatar, occupied chair, blocking character collider, or ongoing player interaction remains. The player is not simulated as an offline seated NPC.
+- On disconnect, **abort/cancel the in-progress player interaction and release its locks/seat/control**: cockpit navigation, storage and Fabricator interfaces, Core access, mining actions, construction interactions or other actively used modules. Do not automatically resume any of these upon reconnect.
+- Previously completed resource transfers or gathered litres remain committed. Already queued, self-running Fabricator jobs and automatic Core conversion are independent machine processes: closing the player's interface **does not undo or cancel them**. No halfway/duplicate resource transactions are permitted.
+- Persist the last safe **non-interaction** position in its appropriate coordinate frame. If disconnect occurs **during an interaction**, persist a spawn point **beside the interacted object/module**, not on the chair or inside its interaction spot. This applies to cockpit, Fabricator, Core, storage, mining and future modules.
+- Clear held movement/steering commands and **active pilot authority** on disconnect; never give another connected player owner-only navigation permission merely because the owner is absent. Ship motion and offline powered-module behavior follow existing authoritative ship/offline contracts; client view changes do not authorize changes to ship physics.
+- On reconnect, restore the player in **2D normal gameplay**, with no menu/mining/navigation interaction resumed and no occupied pilot chair. Multiplayer presence and collision return only after a valid spawn has been resolved.
+
+## Precise reconnect location
+
+| Last state | Saved location / reconnect |
+| --- | --- |
+| On a planet, not using an object | **Same exact surface point** on the **same planet**. Persist canonical planet/body ID and a **planet-fixed surface-relative** anchor, not an obsolete inertial world XYZ that would drift as the planet moves/rotates. |
+| On a planet, actively interacting | Cancel interaction and return **beside that resource/object**, in a valid reachable surface location. |
+| Inside a live ship, not interacting | **Same ship-relative interior point**, on the **same ship**, even if the ship has moved through space while the player was away. |
+| Inside a live ship, operating a module or chair | Cancel/release interaction and reconnect **standing next to that object**, in ship-local space. |
+| Ship containing offline player is damaged but still exists | Reconnect on the ship as above; ship-wide nonfatal damage does not itself kill the offline player. |
+| Ship containing offline player is destroyed | **Offline death**; do not spawn at the wreck or transport the player to a saved planet. |
+
+An invalid or obstructed stored point must never create an overlapping/unsafe avatar. Exact fallback placement for changed planetary surfaces, moved/removed furniture or blocked approach points is a **future design task**, not permission to relocate the player to an unrelated planet or ship.
+
+## Offline death and restart
+
+- During disconnect, the server/persistent world tracks the player's **last anchored location and current alive/dead outcome**, even though the avatar is absent.
+- **If the player was aboard a ship when disconnected and that ship is wholly destroyed while they remain offline, that character is dead.** Record a durable terminal/death result, not a merely missing ship reference.
+- On next reconnect, **do not spawn** that character. First display the clear notification: **“You died while disconnected.”** Explain that the ship they were aboard was destroyed, then begin a **fresh run from Salimon's normal starting state**, applying existing permadeath rules.
+- A player whose last saved location is on a planet **is not killed merely because their ship elsewhere is destroyed**. Nonlethal ship-wide damage to the ship containing an offline player also does not trigger this death rule.
+- Preserve the destroyed ship's world/wreck/salvage consequences under their own existing game systems; do not turn the wreck into an automatic respawn point. The same destruction event must not apply death or reset repeatedly.
+
+## Current ship-damage scope (simplification)
+
+**For the present/forthcoming 2D multiplayer gameplay scope, damage and destruction are ship-wide, not per-room or per-module.** The ship can take nonfatal damage as one vessel; if destruction occurs, it affects the **entire ship**. There is **no presently active partial room loss, detachable compartment survival, or offline occupant relocation between intact rooms**.
+
+Past native implementation documents describing localized cell, module, door or room damage are historical or **deferred future mechanics**. Preserve them for a later design review rather than applying them to the present design. The question of what happens to an offline player if only their room is destroyed is **explicitly deferred**, since partial-room destruction is not in scope.
+
+## Invariants, implementation and deferred discussion
+
+- One cockpit seat has at most one active occupant; one ship has at most one authorized active pilot; ship owner-only navigation remains protected.
+- View switching is a client presentation state change; the authoritative player stays physically inside the ship when seated, and ship motion persists independently.
+- Disconnect must atomically release occupancy/interaction locks and save a valid planet-fixed or ship-local re-entry anchor. It must not leave an offline physical player in the world.
+- Reconnect checks terminal offline death **before** spawning, resuming commands or presenting controls.
+- No implementation is authorized by this document alone; the active `client/` navigation-only radar has no 2D gameplay, cockpit avatar, live multiplayer, server persistence or module seating.
+- **Still to design later:** exact cockpit input key/animation timing, valid-adjacent spawn fallback when a saved spot changes, server timing/race handling, full power/zero-G seating safety, multiplayer interaction with an occupied pilot, reconnect if a ship is transferred/removed without destruction, and eventual localized hull/room/module damage.
+
+## Review examples / acceptance scenarios (future)
+
+1. Two connected players aboard the Scout: owner enters 3D navigation, observer still sees owner's character seated in the 2D cockpit; another occupant cannot claim the same chair.
+2. Normal navigation exit returns the owner to 2D **standing**; power loss returns them to 2D **seated**; restored power does not force 3D open.
+3. Disconnect during cockpit navigation removes the avatar and releases the chair/control; reconnect places them standing beside the desk in 2D.
+4. Disconnect on a rotating/moving planet returns to identical planet-fixed surface coordinates, not inertial-space coordinates.
+5. Disconnect in a coasting/traveling ship returns to the same ship-local point despite movement.
+6. Disconnect during active mining or inventory transfer cancels the active action, keeps already committed output, and returns beside the object without duplicating resources.
+7. Offline ship-wide nonfatal damage permits normal reconnect aboard; **whole-ship destruction** produces a one-time offline-death notice and fresh start instead of spawning in wreckage.
+8. Disconnect on a planet survives destruction of a separate ship; no unrelated death.

+# Resource inventory, gathering and ship processing — strict top-down 2D
+
+**Status: approved gameplay direction (2026-11-04); implementation pending.** The browser client is currently navigation-only. The TypeScript inventory foundation from PR #756 implements a 10 kg / 10 L starting inventory with **integer kilograms per unit** and is **not yet updated** for the newly approved fractional-kg/whole-litre design, ship storage, or continuous Core processing. Do not treat historical native physical-fragment behavior as current 2D gameplay.
+
+## Resource representation and player gathering
+
+- Raw resources are **stacked in whole litres**, not carried as physical fragments. Resource quantities and mining/source depletion are whole-litre increments; no fractional litre can enter an inventory.
+- Each resource type specifies **mass per litre**; fractional kilograms are allowed (e.g. 0.5 kg/L). Use **integer grams per litre** and integer litre quantities internally to avoid floating-point inventory drift. Display kg and L independently.
+- Starting player inventory: **10 kg maximum weight AND 10 L maximum volume**, enforced simultaneously. Future inventory capacity upgrades are possible; their costs/tier values are not defined.
+- The player leaves the Scout, approaches a rock/plant/other harvestable source, equips the mining tool and mines **1 L per second** while the interaction is valid. Suitable gathering interactions for other resource categories need the same capacity and depletion rules.
+- Credit only the litres fitting BOTH remaining limits and remaining source quantity, debiting the corresponding persistent source in the same authoritative operation. Uncollected material remains at the source; no fragments, growing spheres or physical fragment piles are created.
+- Interaction distance, animation/interrupt rules, partial-second progress, tool upgrades, resource-density catalog and source exhaustion visuals require later design/implementation.
+
+## Initial ship-side resource capacities
+
+| Destination | Starting weight capacity | Starting volume capacity | Operation |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Player inventory | 10 kg | 10 L | Collect and transport |
+| One built-in Scout storage container | 50 kg | 50 L | Store and retrieve raw resources |
+| Fabricator input buffer | 50 kg | 50 L | Supply recipes; withdraw unused inputs |
+| Energy Core raw-material buffer | 50 kg | 50 L | Feed energy conversion; withdraw unconsumed inputs |
+
+- Capacities are **independent per inventory/buffer**, with both weight and volume checked. Each may hold mixed resource types up to its combined limits.
+- The player can deposit and withdraw **unused** material from the general container, Fabricator and Core. Material committed to a queued Fabricator job or already converted by the Core is not withdrawable.
+- Storage-container construction and upgrades, Fabricator-buffer upgrades and Core-buffer upgrades are **future design discussions**; no recipes, tiers or costs are set here.
+- Transfers must conserve exact whole litres and associated mass without duplication. The transfer UI, whether module-to-module transfers are allowed, partial-transfer UX and how a partly converted active Core batch is treated on withdrawal remain to be finalized.
+- Player and ship resource mass must be counted once in applicable physics. General storage is distinct from physical furnishings and separately equipped tools/consumables.
+
+## Fabricator
+
+- The Fabricator has a 50 kg / 50 L reserved resource-input buffer at game start; unused materials can be retrieved.
+- Preserve the earlier crafting contract: jobs reserve/consume their ingredients on queue, operate one at a time, pause without power, and deliver finished consumables/items to the output tray. Resources already committed to a job cannot be recovered by withdrawing them from the input buffer.
+- Replacing legacy physical-fragment intake with inventory transfers is future implementation work. Fabricator capacity-upgrade behavior is deferred.
+
+## Energy Core — approved processing model
+
+- The Core starts with a **separate 50 kg / 50 L raw-material buffer**, independent of the Core's stored energy capacity (joules). Unconsumed raw resources can be withdrawn.
+- Material is selected **automatically by highest energy yield first**. The precise comparison metric when densities differ (yield per kg vs yield per whole litre) and deterministic tie-breaking still require an explicit design decision; do not silently claim either ranking is approved.
+- The Core processes **whole-litre input batches with continuous energy output over time**, not instantaneous full-batch energy grants. The energy reserve can be charged while a batch is being processed.
+- **The Core has a fixed maximum energy-generation POWER, measured in watts (J/s).** Actual conversion is bounded by this power rate, available convertible energy, and free energy-storage capacity. A more energy-rich litre can take longer to finish at the same maximum power.
+- Conversion **automatically pauses** when the energy reserve is full, preserving remaining unconverted energy/material, and **automatically resumes** as energy capacity becomes available. It must not discard fuel or generated energy simply because the reserve is full.
+- **The maximum generation power is upgradeable in the future.** This is distinct from upgrading the Core's raw-material buffer capacity or energy-storage capacity.
+- **Design deliberately deferred:** The initial maximum generation power (in MW), the upgrade mechanism, upgrade tiers, maximum upgradeable rate, required resources/costs, prerequisites, and exact power/progress behavior must be **discussed and defined in a later design session**. This document does not authorize adopting old native conversion values or any example number as the new starting rate.
+- Also deferred: how a partially converted 1 L batch is reserved/represented, whether it occupies original capacity throughout processing, what can be withdrawn during processing, save/resume and interruption details, and exact priority/tie-breaking semantics. Preserve material-energy conservation regardless.
+
+## Persistence, authority and current implementation gap
+
+- Source depletion and inventory credit must be authoritative and atomic so interruption, repeated input, saving/reloading or future multiplayer cannot create duplicate resources.
+- Quantities are whole litres; densities use integer grams/litre. Current `client/src/resourceInventory.ts` still enforces whole kilograms per resource unit. Updating it, its tests and the future 2D interaction system is **separate future work**, not completed by this document.
+- Save data for inventories, active Core batch progress, energy reserve and world depletion must be versioned and validated. The existing navigation-only client has none of these machine or 2D integrations.
+- Older native Core fueling, physical-fragment construction refunds and storage/harvesting implementation notes remain historical only; they are not proof of 2D migration.
+
+## Open design questions for later discussion
+
+1. Initial fixed generation power (MW) and its **upgradeable rate progression**, separate from energy-storage upgrades.
+2. Core priority yield metric (per litre versus per kilogram), deterministic tie-breaks, and currently processing batch behavior.
+3. Core active-batch reservation, withdrawal, interruption and persistence.
+4. Mining tool reach, interruption and partial-second progress; actual resource densities and types.
+5. Storage/transfer UI, direct module transfer policy, and capacity upgrade tiers for inventory/storage/Fabricator/Core.
